episode_title: AH118 - Chemo, Cars, & Where Health Plan Savings May be Hiding, with Brian Cotter

real_qa.q: What was the price drop for oxaliplatin (Eloxatin) between 2012 and Q1 2026 after converting from brand to generic?
real_qa.r: In 2012, oxaliplatin was a brand drug with an ASP price of $2,053 for a 200 milligram dose. By Q1 2026, the price dropped to $9.40, representing a drop of over 99%. However, price variation persists in the market—one hospital's website listed the drug at $29,595, while Medicare would reimburse less than ten dollars.

real_qa.q: How much can plan sponsors save by redirecting chemotherapy patients to lower-cost, high-quality providers with direct contracts?
real_qa.r: One plan sponsor implemented a transportation program moving members to a preferred medical center where chemotherapy prices were around 100% of Medicare, compared to local options priced at 500% and above Medicare. This strategy saved 80% on chemotherapy costs for every member successfully transported to the preferred provider.
real_qa.requete: chemotherapy patient transportation cost savings medical center

real_qa.q: How many Medicare J codes for specialty drugs on the medical benefit showed price drops in Q1 2025 to Q1 2026?
real_qa.r: Between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026, 431 drugs had price drops, with some dropping up to 99%. From Q1 2026 to Q3 2026 (first three quarters of the year), 348 drugs had price drops in the medical benefit.
real_qa.requete: Medicare J codes price drops 2025 2026 medical benefit

real_qa.q: What is specialty pharmacy drug spending as a percentage of total plan spend, and how has it grown?
real_qa.r: Specialty drug spend is now between 55-60% of total pharmacy spend. Pharmacy spend overall represents 25-30% of total plan spend, making specialty drugs a significant and rapidly growing portion of employer healthcare expenditures.
real_qa.requete: specialty drug spend percentage total plan 55% 60%

real_qa.q: Why is data validation critical when using price transparency files and claims data to identify drug pricing opportunities?
real_qa.r: Brian emphasizes: assume all data is incorrect until proven otherwise. Every reference data set, claims data, pharmacy data, and benchmark data must be validated for accuracy and completeness. He has found that in every analysis, every reference data set was incorrect to some level, which is why building trust and credibility in data before feeding it into tools or AI systems is essential.
real_qa.requete: healthcare data validation price transparency claims accuracy

real_qa.q: What assumption about biosimilars entering the market is often incorrect when designing benefit programs?
real_qa.r: A common assumption is that biosimilars are always lower cost than the reference drug. However, while biosimilars have dropped reference drug costs and benefited patients, at the current time the reference drug may actually be significantly lower cost than the biosimilar. Plan sponsors must analyze current pricing to determine the actual lowest-cost option rather than relying on this assumption.
real_qa.requete: biosimilar always lower cost reference drug assumption
